bundleDescription:
- **Capability**: define product roles, how each role is obtained, and the concrete operations each role is allowed or explicitly forbidden to perform, and optional single-parent permission inheritance.
- **Resolves**: S/T gaps where actors are known but authorization boundaries, target ranges, runtime conditions, or extra verification remain unclear.
- **Candidate when**: different users or service identities use the product differently, a flow/page contains protected actions, or the user explicitly asks for roles, permissions, RBAC, or access control.
- **Do not infer**: a job title, flow lane, persona, or page visitor is not automatically a product role; do not invent organization levels or enterprise separation-of-duties rules.
- **Output**: `role_access` panel — editable roles with assignment rules and local permissions and an optional same-source inheritance graph with read-only ancestor permission sources.
empty: Add a role, then explain who receives it and what it can do.
title: Role name
assignmentHelp: Choose how this role is granted. Only Other requires your own rule.
assignmentExample: For example: granted on invitation and revoked on leaving the project
capabilityExample: For example: approve orders or view project members
conditionExample: For example: only customers assigned to this person and still being followed up
customHelp: Explain what else must happen before the action
policiesHelp: Each permission allows or denies one capability. Add an applicability condition only when necessary.
guidance: Check what each role can do and which data it can access, looking for excessive or missing permissions. Set one source role only when reuse is needed; grants remain independent.
graphHint: Connect the child to its source role. Return to details for local permissions and read-only inherited sources.
inheritanceHelp: Inherited permissions retain their original applicability, confirmation and identity verification. Role assignment and conflict precedence are not inherited.
